summary: Array cleanup: when this+0xA8 (array block pointer) is non-null, frees per-element resources, then frees the whole block. For each of this+0xA4 elements (stride 148 bytes): if element+76 is non-null it is freed via FreeWrapper_7bcf; if element+144 is non-null, EmptyStub_7470 is called on it first and then it is freed. The block carries a count prefix at array_ptr-4; every 148-byte slot is visited backwards via EmptyStub_7470, then FreeWrapper_7bcf frees the block starting at array_ptr-4. Finally this+0xA8 is nulled and 0 is returned.

operations.description: Outer guard: entire cleanup runs only when this+0xA8 (array block pointer) is non-null.
Per-element guard: guard:0 checks this+0xA4 (element count) > 0 before running the element loop.
do-while loop over this+0xA4 elements, walking the array with 148-byte stride.
For each element, guard on element+76 being non-null before freeing it.
Free element+76 via FreeWrapper_7bcf when it is non-null.
For each element, guard on element+144 being non-null before teardown.
Call EmptyStub_7470 on element+144 as a per-element teardown step.
Free element+144 via FreeWrapper_7bcf after the stub call.
Advance element base by the 148-byte stride each iteration.
Read the element count from the allocator header at array_ptr-4 and compute the end pointer array_ptr + 148 * count.
Backward loop over the block: call EmptyStub_7470 on each 148-byte slot from the last down to the first.
Free the whole block via FreeWrapper_7bcf starting at array_ptr-4 (header plus slots).
Null this+0xA8 (array block pointer) once cleanup finishes.
